record.paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
record.original_question: What quantitative theoretical model can explain why, in SPS and similar hadron-collider observations, proton losses became more sensitive to high-order resonances when the opposing anti-proton bunch emittance was reduced to nearly match the proton emittance, even though the beam-beam parameter was about 40% lower?

evidence.quote: A quantitative theoretical model to explain these observations has not yet been developed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two counter-rotating bunched hadron beams (a proton bunch and an antiproton bunch) interacting at one or more crossing points in a circular collider. The strength of the long-range and head-on beam-beam force experienced by a test proton is characterized by the linear beam-beam parameter
  ξ = N r_p β* / (4π γ σ²),
where N is the opposing antiproton bunch population, r_p the classical proton radius, γ the relativistic factor, β* the optical β-function at the interaction point, and σ the rms transverse size of the opposing (antiproton) bunch. Assume the proton bunch has fixed transverse rms emittance ε_p and the antiproton bunch has rms emittance ε_a, with σ² ∝ ε_a at the interaction point.

Empirical observation in collider operation has shown the following: when ε_a ≫ ε_p (large antiproton emittance), proton losses driven by nonlinear betatron resonances of order ≥ 10 are weak; when ε_a is reduced so that ε_a ≈ ε_p, proton losses on these high-order resonances become substantially stronger, even though the increase of σ caused by the smaller ε_a makes the nominal beam-beam parameter ξ approximately 40% lower than in the large-ε_a configuration.

Develop a quantitative theoretical model — based on the nonlinear single-particle dynamics of a proton in the field of a Gaussian (or arbitrary radially symmetric) opposing bunch, including the dependence of resonance driving terms, dynamic aperture, and diffusion rates on the ratio ε_p/ε_a — that predicts and explains this enhancement of high-order resonance-driven proton losses as ε_a is decreased toward ε_p, despite the simultaneous reduction of ξ by roughly 40%. The model should reproduce, at least at the scaling level, the experimentally observed sensitivity of proton lifetime to high-order resonance tunes as a function of the emittance ratio.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches return general literature on beam-beam effects in proton-antiproton colliders (SPS, Tevatron) and on high-order resonance-driven losses with unequal emittances, but no source explicitly providing a quantitative theoretical model that reproduces the observed enhanced sensitivity to high-order resonances when the opposing-bunch emittance is reduced toward the proton emittance while ξ drops ~40%. The current status of a closed-form/quantitative model for this specific phenomenon could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Beam-beam Effects in Tevatron
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses beam-beam-driven losses, high-order resonances, and emittance dependence in hadron colliders without providing a closed quantitative model for the unequal-emittance SPS observation.
status_evidence.claim: Reviews beam-beam phenomenology relevant to the question but does not present a verified quantitative model for the specific unequal-emittance loss enhancement.

status_evidence.title: Chapter 8 Beam–Beam Effects, Shiltsev & Valishev
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of beam-beam effects in hadron colliders including resonance driving terms and dynamic aperture studies.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general framework but no explicit quantitative model resolving the SPS unequal-emittance high-order resonance sensitivity.

status_evidence.title: Proton-Antiproton Collider (CERN)
status_evidence.snippet: Reports lifetime sensitivity to 10th-order resonances and effects of unequal antiproton bunch emittances on lifetimes in the SPS collider.
status_evidence.claim: Documents the empirical phenomenon but does not supply a quantitative theoretical explanation.
